title: Source-library etale adjoint locality over arbitrary schemes
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $u:U\to X$ a separated quasi-compact etale morphism of arbitrary schemes, and $f:X\to Y$, $h:U\to Y$ morphisms with $h=fu$. Suppose f and h admit open-immersion/proper compactifications. Let $Rf^!$ and $Rh^!$ be right adjoints of their chosen unbounded compact-support functors, and $Lu^*$ the derived inverse image, equal to the degreewise exact inverse image. There exists a natural isomorphism $Lu^*Rf^!\cong Rh^!$. The scheme, morphism, and functor notions used here are those of [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 0GKM, lemma-Rf-shriek-for-quasi-finite; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0F4L, graph-extension argument. The arbitrary-base unbounded extension is proved by the agent using the recorded Lean APIs.

proof.text: Choose a compactification U to Z to Y of h. The graph of u gives U to Z times_Y X, whose projection to X is proper. This graph is an immersion since its composite with the projection to Z is the open immersion of the compactification. Since u is quasi-compact, this immersion/proper factorization supplies a compactification of u. This is the three-line application of HasCompactification.of_isImmersion in the attached proof.
For this compactification identify Ru_! with D(u_{Sigma!}). The exact sum-extension/inverse-image adjunction descends degreewise, so Ru_! is left adjoint to Lu^*.

Compose this adjunction with Rf_! adjoint to Rf^!. Use compact-support composition to identify the composite left adjoint with Rh_!. Uniqueness of right adjoints gives the claimed isomorphism; replace D(u^*) by Lu^* using exactness.

theorem nonempty_iso_rightDerivedUpperShriek_comp_leftDerivedUpperStar_of_etale
    {U X Y : Scheme.{u}} (u : U ⟶ X) [Etale u] [IsSeparated u] [QuasiCompact u]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : U ⟶ Y) (w : u ≫ f = h) [HasCompactification f]
    [HasCompactification h] :
    Nonempty (R(f)^![ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ] ⋙ L((u)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ]) ≅
      R(h)^![ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ])
